model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x AFFO margin less SBC = house AFFO; D&A, capex, tax, leases and working capital all zero because they are already inside AFFO; net debt NOT deducted because AFFO is after net interest)

historical_growth.eps_basis: REPORTED AFFO per diluted share, NOT GAAP EPS: FY2022 $29.56 (2,714/91.828) -> FY2025 $38.33 (3,761/98.123) = 9.0% 3yr; FY2021 $27.11 (2,451/90.409) -> FY2025 = 9.0% over 4 years (reported as the '5yr' figure; FY2020 AFFO is not in the extracted filings). House AFFO per share (SBC deducted): FY2022 $25.16 -> FY2025 $33.25 = 9.7% 3yr; FY2021 $23.08 -> FY2025 = 9.5% 4yr. GAAP EPS (FY2022 $7.69 -> FY2025 $13.79, 21.5% CAGR) is after ~$2.0B of D&A and swings on gains, impairments and tax items; it is not used.
historical_growth.equity_basis: Stockholders' equity FY2022 $11,506M -> FY2025 $14,156M (3yr); FY2020 $10,634M -> FY2025 (5yr). Inflated by $2.5B of ATM issuance in FY2023-24 and depressed by the REIT distribution requirement (dividends ~$1.8B/yr), so it is neither a retained-earnings compounding series nor a revaluation series; recorded as a cross-check only.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: HOUSE AFFO (reported AFFO less SBC), $M: FY2021 2,087 (2,451-364); FY2022 2,310 (2,714-404); FY2023 2,612 (3,019-407); FY2024 2,894 (3,356-462); FY2025 3,263 (3,761-498). 3yr FY2022->FY2025 = 12.2%; the '5yr' figure is the 4-year FY2021->FY2025 CAGR of 11.8% (FY2020 AFFO not in the extracted filings). Reported AFFO CAGRs: 11.5% 3yr, 11.3% 4yr -- house AFFO grew FASTER than reported because SBC (5.5% -> 5.4% of revenue) grew slower than AFFO; SBC is not eating the growth. Per-share house AFFO compounded at 9.5-9.7%, the gap to the total being ~2%/yr of ATM and SBC issuance.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Average of the base-case revenue growth path over FY2027-FY2031 (9.5, 9.0, 8.5, 7.5, 6.5): the FY2026 guidance (+12.2%, inflated ~1pp by one-off fees) fading through the 8.3-9.0% historical revenue CAGR toward 3% terminal. Management's stated multi-year algorithm (10-13% revenue growth through 2029 per the Analysis JSON) is treated as the bull path, not the base. Equity CAGR is not used (see equity_basis).
historical_growth.notes: Equity CAGR (7.2% 3yr) is within 30% of both revenue (8.3%) and AFFO/share (9.0%), so no divergence flag. The honest organic figure is house AFFO per share at ~9.5%/yr: total house AFFO compounded ~12% but ~2%/yr of that was bought with new shares (ATM) on top of the ~$4B/yr of new debt. Bookings momentum (annualized gross bookings $533M in Q3-2026, +35% YoY; MRR double-digit growth four quarters running) argues the FY2027-28 growth can hold near the top of history; the rising interest line ($385M -> $462M 9M YoY) is what the margin path has to absorb.

scenario_narratives.base: Equinix delivers the thrice-raised FY2026 guidance (revenue ~$10.35B, AFFO ~$4.36B, AFFO/share ~$43.91) and then compounds revenue at 9.5% fading to 3% over ten years as the AI-driven capacity cycle matures. The AFFO margin steps down ~0.8pp in FY2027 as 2026's one-off JV and non-recurring fees roll off, then drifts up to 42.5% as EBITDA margin expansion (toward the low 50s) is mostly offset by the interest on ~$2-3B/yr of new debt that funds the gap between $5-6B of capex and retained AFFO. SBC (~5.4% of revenue) is charged as a real cost and the share count grows 0.8%/yr for ATM issuance. The value is the resulting house-AFFO stream capitalised at an 8.5% USD cost of equity with a 3% terminal rate -- an 18.7x exit multiple against ~26x today, so the base case assumes the market stops paying a growth premium once growth normalises.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI inference and hybrid-cloud interconnection demand proves durable and broad-based: bookings keep growing 20-35%, management's 10-13% revenue algorithm is delivered through 2029 and fades only slowly, pricing strength (MRR per cabinet +5-12%/yr) and Fabric growth lift the AFFO margin to 45%, and lower rates plus more JV-funded hyperscale builds reduce the interest drag. House AFFO per share compounds at low double digits for five years. The terminal multiple is 20.7x house AFFO at a 3.5% terminal rate -- still below today's multiple, but the ten years of compounding before it carry the value.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI capex cycle cools from 2027: hyperscalers self-build or go to wholesale specialists, enterprise AI deployments disappoint, and Equinix's accelerated 2026 cabinet deliveries land in a softer market, pulling utilization into the low 70s and ending pricing power in a market with 2,400+ competitors. Revenue growth falls to 4-5% by FY2029 and 2.5% thereafter. Meanwhile the $25B+ debt stack keeps repricing higher as 3.2-3.5% notes mature, so interest compounds faster than EBITDA and the AFFO margin gives back 3.5pp to 38.5%. The ATM is used harder to protect the dividend. Exit at 15x house AFFO, the 2022-23 data-center REIT trough multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Equinix is valued as a stream of house AFFO -- the company's own AFFO less the stock-based compensation it adds back -- capitalised at an 8.5% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because AFFO is already after the ~$650M/yr interest run-rate. GAAP earnings (after ~$2B of depreciation), book value (distorted by REIT distributions and ATM issuance) and reported free cash flow (negative through a $5-6B/yr expansion capex programme) are all set aside. The base case is essentially the FY2026 guidance fading from ~10% to 3% growth with a roughly flat AFFO margin; it values the business below the current price, which means the market is capitalising Equinix at a materially lower cost of equity, a higher terminal growth rate, or management's full 10-13% algorithm sustained. The street basis (SBC treated as non-cash, i.e. Equinix's reported AFFO) is reported alongside; the gap between house and street is ~5.4% of revenue per year of SBC and is a material fraction of the per-share value. The reader should hold one caveat: AFFO capitalisation credits all the growth that expansion capex buys while charging only the interest and dilution that fund it -- it assumes the ~$5B/yr being deployed earns its cost of capital.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: at an 8.5% cost of equity and 3% terminal growth the terminal value is roughly 60% of the base value; every 50bp on the rate moves it ~9-10%, and the current price implies a rate closer to 7.5% on the base flows.

AI demand durability and hyperscaler self-build: the revenue growth path is the single biggest driver; the gap between the bear (7% fading to 2.5%) and bull (12% fading to 3.5%) paths is most of the per-share spread.

Interest drag: total indebtedness grew $3.8B in nine months to $25.2B; 3.2-3.5% notes maturing 2027-29 refinance at 5%+. The flat-to-rising AFFO margin assumes EBITDA expansion keeps outrunning interest; if it does not, the bear margin path (-3.5pp) is the result.

Expansion capex is not charged: $5-6B/yr sits outside AFFO. If the incremental builds earn below the cost of capital (over-building into a cooling cycle, power-constrained sites), the growth path is too generous for the risk taken.
SBC treatment: ~$555M/yr (5.4% of revenue) separates the house and street values; the market prices Equinix on the street definition.
Equity issuance: 0.8%/yr of ATM/forward dilution is assumed; a prolonged period of negative FCF with tighter credit markets would push this higher (FY2024 was 2.0%).
FX: ~61% of revenue is non-USD; a strong dollar reduces reported revenue and AFFO without changing the underlying business.

data_sources.financials: EQIX Metrics CSV / core_metrics and kpis (XBRL-sourced financials; AFFO, FFO, adjusted EBITDA, bookings, utilization, segment revenue KPIs), FY2025 total_debt corrected to $21.4B total indebtedness via make fix. Q3-2026 10-Q (EQIX_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt): AFFO/FFO reconciliation lines 4585-4615, diluted shares line 2706, cover-page shares line 2497, forward sale table lines 3728-3749, total indebtedness line 5154, interest expense line 2694. FY2025 10-K (EQIX_Annual_FY2025.txt): AFFO reconciliation lines 4242-4276 (AFFO 3,761/3,356/3,019; SBC 498/462/407; recurring capex 284/250/219), interest expense line 4185, diluted shares line 4798, ATM issuance lines 4842-4871, total indebtedness line 3472. data_sources.qualitative: EQIX_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): FY2026 guidance as raised 28-Oct-2026, long-term 10-13% revenue algorithm, bookings, xScale JV structure, risk register.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E revenue at the midpoint of the 28-Oct-2026 guidance range ($10.325-10.365B, raised for the third consecutive quarter; 9M-2026 actual $7.640B, Q4 guided $2.684-2.724B). FY0 is the guidance year rather than FY2025 actuals (revenue $9,217M) because the fiscal year is ten-twelfths complete at the valuation date and guided to a +/-0.2% range; using FY2025 as FY0 would discount an essentially banked year by a full period. Revenue is the DRIVER line; the flow that is valued is AFFO (42.1% of FY2026E revenue reported, 36.8% after SBC).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 99,277k weighted-average diluted shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q EPS note, includes RSU dilution; 98,988,318 basic outstanding at 27-Oct-2026 cover page) PLUS 465k shares under the forward sale agreements executed May-Jun 2026 under the 2024 ATM Program (physical settlement by Jan-2027 at $1,073.58, $500M proceeds) = 99.74M. The forward shares are contracted issuance, not SBC, so they belong in the count. annual_share_growth_pct 0.8% models continued ATM/forward equity issuance to fund the capex program (FY2023 1.02M shares/$734M, FY2024 1.97M/$1,673M, FY2025 0.11M/$99M, 2026 0.47M/$500M forward: ~0.9M shares/yr average, ~0.8% of the count); this is genuine non-SBC issuance. SBC-driven dilution is NOT in the count: SBC is expensed in the flows (sbc_pct_path), charged once.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is AFFO, which is already AFTER interest expense ($527M FY2025; $462M 9M-2026 vs $385M 9M-2025, Q3-2026 run-rate ~$650M/yr) and after interest income. Deducting the balance-sheet net debt on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only: total indebtedness $25.2B at 30-Sep-2026 inclusive of finance lease liabilities (~$2.35B) and gross of issuance costs (10-Q liquidity section), vs $21.4B at 31-Dec-2025 on the same basis (the corrected FY2025 CSV figure); senior notes principal $22.6B after $5.4B issued in 9M-2026. Cash and equivalents $2,362M (CSV, Q3 2026); cash plus short-term investments $3.6B per the 10-Q. Undrawn $5.5B revolver. Net debt / FY2026E adjusted EBITDA ~4.1x on the $5.31B guidance midpoint.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E HOUSE AFFO = guided AFFO midpoint $4,360M ($4.340-4.380B, 28-Oct-2026) LESS FY2026E stock-based compensation $555M (9M-2026 $414M per the AFFO reconciliation + Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of $141M). Equinix's AFFO definition ADDS BACK stock-based compensation expense (Q3-2026 10-Q AFFO reconciliation: +$141M Q3, +$414M 9M) and deducts only recurring capital expenditures ($149M 9M-2026; $284M FY2025); house policy treats SBC as a real cost, so it is deducted again here. For reference FY2025 actual: reported AFFO $3,761M, SBC $498M, house AFFO $3,263M ($33.25/diluted share); 9M-2026 reported AFFO $3,389M (+17.5%) includes a one-time atNorth JV fee in Q3 (reported +20% vs +14% normalized) and a Q2 non-recurring revenue spike ($248M vs ~$115M run-rate), so ~1pp of the FY2026E AFFO margin is non-repeating -- see the Y1 margin step-down. This is NOT the CSV free_cash_flow (FY2025 -$400M; 9M-2026 -$801M): reported FCF is after $4.3-5.5B/yr of expansion capex and is structurally negative during the AI build-out.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026E AFFO attributable to common stockholders at the guidance midpoint (company definition, SBC added back). FFO 9M-2026 $2,470M; FY2025 FFO $2,668M. GAAP net income ($1,350M FY2025) is after ~$2.0B of D&A and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q AFFO reconciliation and cash flow statement: stock-based compensation expense $141M Q3-2026, $414M 9M-2026 ($130M / $370M prior year); FY2025 10-K $498M (FY2024 $462M, FY2023 $407M, FY2022 $404M, FY2021 $364M). The AFFO reconciliation line equals the cash-flow add-back; Equinix publishes no separate equity-award-tax line in the reconciliation, and the 'shares purchased' for tax withholding (139k FY2025) are inside the count mechanics, so the add-back is used as the full charge.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $193M (9M-2026 $123M) is left INSIDE AFFO because no cash is added to enterprise value and net debt is not deducted: the matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction (the cash that earns it is netted against the debt whose interest is also inside AFFO).
inputs.buyback_note: No share repurchases since 2014. Equinix is a net ISSUER (ATM programs), which is why annual_share_growth_pct is positive.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026 at guidance midpoint (estimate; fiscal year ends 31-Dec-2026, 9M actuals banked)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:01Z (Nasdaq regular close Friday 6-Nov-2026; Yahoo v8 chart meta; not an after-hours print; valuation date is the following Sunday)
inputs.dividend_note: $5.16/quarter from Q1 2026 (+10% on $4.69), 11th consecutive year of growth; FY2026 cash dividends guided ~$2,037M = ~54% of FY2026E house AFFO, ~47% of reported AFFO.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and no net debt is deducted: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Nov-2026) + 0.85 beta x 5.0% US ERP = 8.45%, rounded to 8.5%. The same 8.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the flows and the weights). Cross-check: at current_price the market capitalises FY2026E reported AFFO/share of $43.91 at 23.1x (4.3% yield) and house AFFO/share of ~$38.15 at 26.5x (3.8% yield); for a 3.8% yield to clear an 8.5% cost of equity the market must be pricing ~5%+ perpetual growth, i.e. the price assumes the AI build-out compounds AFFO/share at high single digits for a decade and then grows above GDP.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease rent ($238M FY2025) is an operating expense inside adjusted EBITDA and AFFO; finance lease interest ($121M FY2025) is inside interest expense and AFFO; finance lease liabilities ($2.35B) are inside the $25.2B total indebtedness recorded for audit. No separate lease charge and no lease liability in the (zero) net debt: one treatment, inside the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: AFFO is attributable to common stockholders (NCI share of $2M 9M-2026 already removed). xScale joint ventures (GIC/CPP 75% / Equinix 25% US venture; PGIM; atNorth 40%) are equity-accounted and enter AFFO via the 'adjustments for FFO/AFFO from unconsolidated joint ventures' lines ($34M 9M-2026). No further NCI adjustment.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row (Equinix is a US REIT since 2015; the per-request route was AFFO capitalisation, confirmed by the methodology: AFFO is already post-interest and post-tax, reported FCF is structurally negative through the capex cycle, and EBITDA-less-capex would value a company spending $5-6B/yr on expansion as worthless). Run on the Drivers/engine route, GPT.AX / CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin = REPORTED AFFO margin (post-interest, post-cash-tax, post-recurring-capex), SBC = Equinix's SBC add-back charged as a % of revenue so that house (SBC expensed) and street (SBC added back, the company's own AFFO) bases are both produced and band_position is meaningful; D&A = 0 (AFFO excludes depreciation by construction), capex = 0 (recurring capex is already deducted inside AFFO; expansion capex is growth capital funded by debt and ATM equity, whose cost enters as the interest drag in the margin path and the 0.8%/yr share growth), cash_tax_rate = 0 (income tax is inside AFFO; the REIT itself pays no US federal tax, TRS and foreign taxes ~$207M cash FY2025 are deducted), working capital = 0, net_debt = 0. CAVEAT the reader should hold: AFFO capitalisation credits the growth that $5-6B/yr of expansion capex buys while charging only the interest on the debt and the dilution from the equity that fund it -- it assumes the incremental capex earns at least its cost of capital, which is the hyperscale/AI demand bet. This is the standard REIT framing and the one the market prices on, but it is more generous than an owner-FCF view would be. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the Friday 6-Nov-2026 Nasdaq regular close. Balance sheet from the 30-Sep-2026 10-Q (filed late Oct-2026), share count from the 27-Oct-2026 cover page plus the outstanding forward sale, FY2025 total_debt in the CSV corrected to $21.4B total indebtedness via make fix.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 still grows 7% on contracted MRR and capacity already sold, then the AI infrastructure cycle cools: hyperscalers self-build or lease wholesale from specialists, the 10-K's own warning that 'the future of AI is still uncertain' comes true, bookings normalise to 2023-24 levels, new cabinets deliver into a softer market (utilization drifts to low-70s%), and pricing power in a 2,400-competitor market fades. Growth settles at 2.5%, roughly inflation.
bear.margin_rationale: AFFO margin gives back 3.5pp to 38.5% (the FY2024 level): interest expense keeps compounding on the $25B+ debt stack (refinancing 3.2-3.5% notes maturing 2027-29 at 5%+) while revenue growth no longer outruns it; power costs and under-utilized new capacity dilute EBITDA margin; FX (61% of revenue non-USD) adds noise. Dividend cover on house AFFO falls toward 1.3x and the ATM has to be used harder.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5% / 2.0% = 15.7x is capped at 15x house AFFO (a 6.7% exit AFFO yield, roughly where data-center REITs traded in the 2022-23 rate shock). Cap binds.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 at 9.5%: FY2026 delivers +12.2% but ~1pp of that is one-off fee revenue (Q2 non-recurring $248M vs ~$115M run-rate; atNorth JV fee Q3), so the underlying run-rate is ~10-11%, and record bookings (+35%) plus ~40% more cabinets delivering in 2026 than planned support high single digits into 2027-28. Then a glide through the 8.3-9.0% historical revenue CAGR toward 3% as the AI capacity cycle matures, utilization (77-78%) absorbs the new builds and the Asia-Pacific/EMEA utilization slack (73-76%) is filled. 10-year average 6.2%; management's 10-13% algorithm is NOT assumed in the base.
base.margin_rationale: This is the REPORTED AFFO / revenue margin (post-interest, post-tax, post-recurring-capex, before the SBC deduction below). History: 37.3% FY2022, 36.9% FY2023, 38.4% FY2024, 40.8% FY2025, 42.1% FY2026E (guidance). Y1 steps DOWN 0.8pp to 41.3% because ~$100-150M of FY2026 AFFO is non-repeating fee income, then drifts up 0.2-0.3pp/yr to 42.5% and holds: adjusted EBITDA margin expansion (46.8% FY2024 -> 49.1% FY2025 -> 51.3% FY2026E guidance; new-generation IBX density, pricing strength) is largely offset by the interest drag of funding a ~$3B/yr gap between capex ($5-6B) and retained AFFO (~$2.3B after dividends) with ~$2.3B/yr of new debt at ~5% (+$115M/yr interest, ~1pp of revenue per year cumulatively). Net +1.2pp over six years versus +5pp over the last three -- deliberately below trend.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC / revenue: 5.5% FY2021, 5.6% FY2022, 5.0% FY2023, 5.3% FY2024, 5.4% FY2025, 5.4% FY2026E. Anchored at the latest actual and declined 0.1pp/yr (slower than the 0.5pp default: SBC has NOT been falling as a share of revenue at Equinix, and AFFO-per-share-linked PSUs scale with the business). Deducting it is what makes this the house basis; the street basis adds it back and equals Equinix's own AFFO.
base.da_rationale: Zero: AFFO excludes real-estate depreciation ($1,070M 9M-2026) and adds back non-real-estate depreciation and amortization by definition; there is no further D&A to deduct or add back.
base.capex_rationale: Zero because recurring capex ($284M FY2025, 3.1% of revenue; $149M 9M-2026) is ALREADY deducted inside AFFO. Expansion capex ($4.3B FY2025; $4.4B 9M-2026; $5-6B FY2026 guidance, excluding xScale JV-level spend) is growth capital, funded by new debt (interest inside the margin path) and ATM equity (the 0.8%/yr share growth); it is what the revenue growth path pays for and is deliberately not charged a second time.
base.tax_rationale: Zero because AFFO is already after income tax ($160M expense FY2025, $207M cash paid: TRS and foreign operating taxes; the REIT itself pays no US federal tax on distributed income). The AFFO 'income tax expense adjustment' line removes only non-cash/one-off tax items.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5% / 3.0% = 18.7x terminal house AFFO (a 5.3% AFFO yield) binds below the 20x cap. Equinix trades at ~26x FY2026E house AFFO (23x reported) today, so the model assumes multiple COMPRESSION of roughly a third over the decade as growth matures -- the implied exit multiple is below today's.

bull.growth_rationale: Management's 10-13% multi-year algorithm is delivered: AI inference and enterprise hybrid-cloud demand keeps annualized gross bookings growing 20%+ (Q3-2026 +35%), pricing keeps strengthening (MRR/cabinet +5-12% across regions in FY2025), Fabric/interconnection compounds at 20%+ (Fabric revenue +24% YoY), the ~1GW of banked powered land converts into capacity sold ahead of delivery, and xScale JV fees recur. Growth holds double digits for four years and fades slowly.
bull.margin_rationale: AFFO margin keeps rising toward 45% as adjusted EBITDA margin reaches the low-to-mid 50s on density and pricing, interconnection mix lifts gross margin, rates ease so refinancing and new issuance cost less, and more of the hyperscale build moves into JVs (fee income without balance-sheet interest). Still a slower expansion than FY2023-26.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5% / 3.5% = 20.7x, inside the 22x cap. Same 8.5% cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows, not a cheaper discount rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates leverage 'high' ($21.4B -> $25.2B total indebtedness in nine months), reported FCF is -$801M for 9M-2026 and will stay negative through the build-out, the 10-K itself calls the future of AI 'uncertain', power availability is an explicit worsening constraint, and the equity story depends on capital markets staying open at acceptable rates. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to hold at once for a decade (AI demand durability, hyperscalers continuing to rent rather than build, power access, rates easing, and the market continuing to pay 20x+ for a maturing REIT). Base 50%: the next two years are largely contracted MRR and capacity already sold, guidance has been raised three quarters running, and the base path already sits below management's own algorithm.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
